look_here_first: Look for a shrub with small crenate leaves that are densely gray-white beneath from stellate hairs. Then confirm dioecious flowers and the 3-lobed capsule; stipule and stamen characters help separate close Bernardia species.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: broadly elliptic to orbiculate leaves with revolute crenate margins

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: abaxial leaf surface grayish-white and densely stellate-pubescent

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: caducous green-to-straw stipules lacking dark resinous exudate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: 3-carpellate pistil with three styles densely penicillate adaxially

lookalikes.differences: B. incana has persistent darkened resinous stipule bases and fewer stamens; B. obovata is greener and more sparsely stellate beneath with a 2-carpellate pistil. Do not identify Bernardia from stellate hairs alone because Croton can look similar.
